# arthron

> A fetch client assembled from plugins. Returns native `Response`; middleware controls flow (can retry via `next`), interceptors transform values. Zero dependencies, ESM + CJS, Node 18+ and browsers.

Import: `import { arthron, retry, timeout, logging, isArthronError, definePlugin } from "arthron";`

## Create

```ts
const api = arthron({
  baseURL?: string,              // prefix for relative paths; required unless you pass absolute URLs
  allowAbsoluteUrls?: boolean,   // default false: an absolute URL must stay on baseURL's origin
  headers?: HeadersInit,         // defaults, per-call headers win (case-insensitive); { name: null } in extend/per-call drops one
  credentials?: RequestCredentials, // NOT set unless you set it
  fetch?: typeof fetch,          // injection for tests/polyfills, resolved per request
  use?: Plugin[],                // plugins, outermost first
  errorMessage?: (data: unknown, res: Response) => string | undefined,
  throwOn?: (res: Response) => boolean, // which non-ok responses reject; also a per-call option
});
```

## Request

```ts
api.get(path, init?) | api.delete(path, init?) | api.head(path, init?)
api.post(path, body?, init?) | api.put(path, body?, init?) | api.patch(path, body?, init?) | api.query(path, body?, init?)   // QUERY = RFC 10008
api.request(path, { method, body?, ...init })      // method is required here
// init = RequestInit minus method/body, plus params?: Record<string, scalar | scalar[] | null | undefined> | URLSearchParams (arrays → repeated keys; object values → TypeError); headers values may be null to drop a default; meta?: ArthronMeta (plugin settings, not sent)
```

Every method returns `Promise<Response>` plus helpers:
`.json<T>()` `.text()` `.blob()` `.arrayBuffer()` `.formData()` `.sse({ maxLineLength?, maxEventSize? }?): AsyncIterable<{event?,data,id?,lastEventId,retry?}> (lastEventId and retry persist across events, per spec; no reconnection)` `.ndjson<T>({ maxLineLength? }?): AsyncIterable<T>` — limits default to 8 Mi characters; exceeding one rejects with RangeError and cancels the body

- Body: string/FormData/Blob/ArrayBuffer/URLSearchParams/ReadableStream sent as-is (matched by type tag, so polyfill/cross-realm instances count; streams get `duplex: "half"`; FormData is sent without content-type so the runtime sets the boundary). Any other value (incl. null) → JSON + `content-type: application/json`; a content type you set must be JSON-ish (else TypeError). Map/Set/iterables/async iterables (Node streams)/functions → TypeError. GET/HEAD with body → TypeError.
- URL: `baseURL` + path by string concatenation (`"https://a/v1" + "/u"` → `https://a/v1/u`). An absolute path must be http(s) and, when baseURL is set, on baseURL's origin — else TypeError, unless `allowAbsoluteUrls: true`; config headers are never sent to another origin. On cross-origin redirects fetch drops Authorization but keeps custom headers (x-api-key) — use `redirect: "error"` where that matters. `params` appended with `&` if a query exists, placed before `#fragment`.
- Argument errors (no baseURL, URL the global fetch cannot parse, BigInt body, missing method) reject the promise with TypeError before fetch; they do not throw synchronously and are never retried. URLs are pre-checked only for the global fetch; an injected `fetch` decides its own URL rules (relative URLs are fine if it accepts them).
- `.sse()`/`.ndjson()`: leaving the loop early cancels the body. `.sse()` drops an event the stream ends inside (spec).

## Errors

```ts
class ArthronError extends Error {
  status: number;        // HTTP status, 0 = network failure
  statusText: string;
  headers: Headers;      // not enumerable
  data: unknown;         // JSON if parseable, else text, else undefined; from at most 64 KiB of body (text if cut)
  response?: Response;   // still readable, holding what was read (≤ 64 KiB); absent for network failure; not enumerable
  request: { url: string; init: RequestInit }; // not enumerable (holds credentials)
  cause?: unknown;       // underlying error for network failure
  toJSON(): { name, message, status, statusText, method, url /* no query/userinfo */, data };
}
isArthronError(e): e is ArthronError
```

- Only `!response.ok` and fetch rejection become ArthronError — and not every non-ok: opaque responses (no-cors) and the 3xx of `redirect: "manual"` are returned; `throwOn(res)` (config or per call) narrows further. An ok response never rejects. Aborts (`AbortError`/`TimeoutError` or any custom `abort(reason)`, including during the error-body read) and exceptions thrown by plugins propagate untouched and skip error interceptors.
- Serializing an ArthronError (JSON.stringify, console.error, error trackers, logging onEvent) never includes request headers, body, query or userinfo. Error messages arthron writes leave the query out too. `message` usually comes from the server body — untrusted text.
- Default message: body `message` → `error` (string) → `error.message` → `detail` → `"Request failed with status N"`. Override with `errorMessage`.

## Plugins

```ts
type Plugin = {
  name?: string;   // identity: use/extend replace a same-named plugin in place; without(name) removes it
  middleware?: (ctx, next: (ctx) => Promise<Response>) => Promise<Response>; // wraps the call; may call next again (retry) or not at all
  request?: (ctx) => ctx;                      // per attempt, before fetch
  response?: (res, ctx) => Response;           // per successful attempt; body is single-use, clone() to peek
  error?: (err: ArthronError, ctx) => ArthronError; // per failed attempt; return value is always thrown
};
type RequestContext = { url: string; init: Omit<RequestInit, "headers"> & { headers: Record<string, string> }; meta: ArthronMeta }; // headers: lowercase record, re-normalized after each request interceptor — spreading is safe
// meta: per-call plugin settings from api.get(path, { meta }), never sent. Built-ins read meta.retry (false | options) and meta.timeout (ms).
// Add keys: declare module "arthron" { interface ArthronMeta { skipAuth?: boolean } }
```

Order: `middleware[0]( middleware[1]( attempt: request interceptors → fetch → response | error interceptors ) )`. Each attempt gets a fresh copy of ctx (headers, and a FormData/URLSearchParams body).

`api.use(...plugins)`, `api.extend(config)` and `api.without(...names)` return NEW clients; the original is unchanged. A named plugin replaces the one with the same name at its position (built-ins: "retry", "timeout", "logging"); unnamed plugins append.

Helpers (identity, for typing): `definePlugin(p)`, `defineMiddleware(m)`, `defineInterceptor.request(f) / .response(f) / .error(f)`.

## Built-in plugins

- `retry({ retries=2, retryOn=[408,429,500,502,503,504], methods=[GET,HEAD,OPTIONS,QUERY,PUT,DELETE], delay=(n)=>Math.random()*300*2**n /* full jitter */, maxRetryAfter=60000, shouldRetry?(error, attempt, ctx) → true|false|undefined, onRetry?(error, attempt, waitMs) })` — re-runs the whole attempt (request interceptors included). Honours Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date). Never retries ReadableStream bodies or aborted requests, nor beyond `retries`; by default never non-ArthronErrors (shouldRetry may opt in, e.g. an inner TimeoutError). With methods: ["POST"], network errors (status 0) are retried too — refuse them with shouldRetry where a duplicate would hurt. Per call: `meta: { retry: false }` or `meta: { retry: { retries: 5 } }`. `retries` must be a whole number ≥ 0 (TypeError otherwise); waits are capped at 2^31-1 ms.
- `timeout(ms, { idle? })` — deadline from attempt start until the body is fully read; `idle` also aborts after that many ms without data (headers or chunks), so `timeout(Infinity, { idle: 30_000 })` never cuts a flowing stream. Rejects with TimeoutError (not ArthronError; retry ignores it). Place after `retry` for per-attempt, before it for total. Per call: `meta: { timeout: ms }` (Infinity lifts it). `Infinity` = no deadline; NaN/negative/>2^31-1 → TypeError. Keeps `res.url`/`redirected`/`type` (through `clone()` too); timers are unref'd.
- `logging({ enabled=true, logger=console, onEvent?, now? })` — start/success/error lines or structured events `{ phase, method, path, status?, ms?, error? }`. Never prints query strings or userinfo. Does not log cancellations.

## Recipes

Auth refresh — single flight, origin-scoped (full version: examples/auth-refresh.ts):
```ts
const auth = (store, origin) => { let refreshing; const bearer = () => store.token() ? `Bearer ${store.token()}` : undefined; return definePlugin({
  name: "auth",
  request: (ctx) => !bearer() || new URL(ctx.url).origin !== origin ? ctx : { ...ctx, init: { ...ctx.init, headers: { ...ctx.init.headers, authorization: bearer() } } },
  middleware: async (ctx, next) => { try { return await next(ctx); } catch (e) { if (!isArthronError(e) || e.status !== 401) throw e; if (e.request.init.headers.authorization === bearer()) { refreshing ??= store.refresh().finally(() => (refreshing = undefined)); await refreshing; } return next(ctx); } },
}); };
```

Reacting to a call's final outcome (error page, domain error) is middleware registered BEFORE retry() — error interceptors run per attempt, including attempts a retry then recovers (see examples/error-page.ts).

Streaming an LLM response:
```ts
for await (const { data } of api.post("/v1/chat/completions", { model, messages, stream: true }).sse()) {
  if (data === "[DONE]") break;          // provider sentinel, not handled by arthron
  const chunk = JSON.parse(data);
}
```

## Non-goals

No request/response key transformation, no caching, no dedupe, no upload progress, no backend-envelope unwrapping. Do those in your adapter layer.
